A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MCP-Flow and contain readable main text, figures, tables, algorithm pseudocode and Appendices A–E. Content can be matched despite substantial layout changes and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original MCP tool-use, retrieval-augmentation and GAIA experiments, plus scaling analyses and weather-server evaluations.

after.justification: V3 retains those experiments and adds human annotation, dataset-quality comparisons and MCP-Flow results on BFCL V3. Its BFCL comparator scores are explicitly attributed to the leaderboard.

M1.justification: The collection algorithm, synthesis stages, fine-tuning and retrieval procedures otherwise match. However, v1 Section 3.3 explicitly filters invalid-response trajectories using DeepSeek-V3; v3 omits this paragraph without clarifying whether the procedure changed or only its documentation was shortened.

E1.justification: V3 adds actual evaluation on BFCL V3, covering external single-turn non-live/live and multi-turn function-calling scenarios (Appendix B.3, Table 10). This substantially extends coverage beyond the retained MCP marketplace, GAIA and weather evaluations; v1 cited BFCL only for its AST metric.

E2.justification: The new BFCL comparison includes Claude-4.5-Sonnet, GPT-5.2, Qwen3-30B, DeepSeek-V3.2, ToolACE-2-8B and TOUCAN-7B, alongside GPT-4.1, using leaderboard scores. ToolACE also joins the quantitative dataset comparison. Existing MCP experiment comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: V3 adds an auxiliary human-evaluation protocol: 300 instances, 100 per split, two independent annotators, and checks of label correctness among ten candidates and tool necessity. Table 8 adds quality/complexity evaluation on 1,000 random samples. Existing splits, training settings and GAIA procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.5 adds a focused label-noise and task-validity audit. Appendix B.2 extends the existing diversity analysis with dataset quality and complexity comparisons. Original tool-count, scaling, cross-marketplace and weather-server analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new two-annotator study specifies an annotation protocol but reports no agreement statistic or uncertainty estimate.

E6.justification: New results include human correctness of 99.00%, 96.00% and 97.25% across the three splits, dataset quality/complexity scores, and BFCL scores of 31.38, 85.58 and 78.09 for MCP-Flow-Qwen3-4B. Existing MCP results and GAIA success/weighted-step values match. V3 removes the raw GAIA step column, including the 2.90 and 6.28 augmented-agent values.

T1.justification: Neither version develops theoretical results or proofs. Algorithm 1 and the existing formal content are unchanged; the added empirical analyses introduce no formal derivations or mathematical guarantees.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: scalable automated MCP data construction, a large training/retrieval dataset, compact fine-tuned models and improved tool use and agentic performance. New experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: V3 adds explicit limitations concerning server degradation, synthetic tasks versus real user behavior, and single-turn data versus extended agentic workflows. It also interprets the new audits and BFCL results as evidence of reliability and generalization. Appendix B.2 overstates consistently superior quality: Table 8 gives LiveMCPBench 8.55 versus MCP-Flow 8.47.

D1.justification: V1's reproducibility statement offers initial anonymous samples and promises a full release; v3 states that all data, code and checkpoints are released through the public repository. V3 also loses the explicit trajectory-filtering detail. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, model versions and prompt content are retained.

R1.justification: V3 adds InfoMosaic-Bench to the contextual comparison in Table 1 and adds citations including KnowledgeSG, FedMABench, MobileA3gent and SWE-agile. These are limited additions; the central positioning around scalable, trainable MCP datasets remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The narrative is largely retained, with shortened passages and renamed sections. Experimental setups become unnumbered introductory material, appendix subsections are reorganized, reproducibility moves under Ethics Statement, and the separate LLM-use disclosure disappears. The affiliation wording is also corrected.

P2.justification: V3 adopts a two-column layout with extensively resized and repositioned displays. Dataset statistics and the crawling illustration move into the appendix, three result tables are added, and the GAIA table is compressed. Existing figures and prompt panels are retained but substantially reflowed.

improvement.justification: The human audit and external BFCL evaluation add useful evidence about dataset reliability and applicability, while explicit limitations and clearer release information improve transparency. The gain is limited by sparse reporting of the new evaluations, the quality overstatement contradicted by Table 8, and omission of trajectory-filtering details and raw GAIA step counts. Overall, the added validation supports a modest improvement.
